story.title: Manchester City Found Guilty of Financial Rule Breaches by Premier League
story.summary: Manchester City has been found guilty of all charges related to breaches of Premier League financial rules from the 2009-10 to 2017-18 seasons, as confirmed by the league. The club expressed disappointment and surprise at the verdict and announced plans to appeal the decision.

explore_lenses.label: What happens to City's season now?
explore_lenses.title: Sanction and appeal come next
explore_lenses.summary: The finding does not itself specify a competitive penalty. The commission must determine a sanction, while Manchester City says it will appeal the opinion.

claims.text: Premier League chief executive Richard Masters said the sanction remains to be decided; the league’s disciplinary framework allows fines, points deductions and other sporting sanctions.
Manchester City said it will pursue available appeals, arguing that the commission’s opinion contains material errors of law, principle and fact.
Under the Premier League process, an Appeal Board may dismiss or allow an appeal, or vary the commission’s order; its proceedings are confidential.

explore_lenses.label: How did Manchester City reach this point?
explore_lenses.title: A nine-season case after a long investigation
explore_lenses.summary: The case concerns alleged financial-rule breaches from 2009-10 through 2017-18. It followed a four-year Premier League investigation and a February 2023 referral to an independent commission.

claims.text: The Premier League charged City in February 2023 after a four-year investigation into conduct during the 2009-10 to 2017-18 seasons.
The league said the independent commission found that City used sham commercial contracts and related arrangements to inflate revenue and reduce costs artificially.
City maintains that it is innocent and says it possesses evidence supporting its position.

explore_lenses.label: What does the verdict change for the league?
explore_lenses.title: It creates a precedent, not an immediate outcome
explore_lenses.summary: The decision establishes liability in this case, but its practical effects on standings, honours or City’s league status depend on the yet-undecided sanction and any appeal.

claims.text: Masters called the decision the most significant in Premier League history and said the league wants to move swiftly through the remaining process to provide certainty for clubs and fans.
The Premier League says serious rule breaches are heard by independent commissions, whose available penalties can range from fines and points deductions to other sporting sanctions.
Any forecast that City will lose points, be expelled, or have past titles altered is premature because the commission has not announced a sanction and City intends to appeal.

story_report.summary: Manchester City has been found guilty of all charges over Premier League financial-rule breaches spanning the 2009-10 to 2017-18 seasons. The club said it was disappointed and surprised by the ruling, maintained its innocence and said it would pursue an appeal, arguing the commission’s opinion contains material errors of law, principle and fact. No sanction has yet been announced, leaving the practical consequences of the decision undetermined.

sections.heading: Premier League Investigation and Findings
sections.body: The Premier League charged City in February 2023 after a four-year investigation into conduct during the nine seasons in question. The league said an independent commission found that the club used sham commercial contracts and related arrangements to inflate revenue and artificially reduce costs. The full written reasoning and evidence record were not included in the reporting consulted.

sections.heading: Sanction and Appeal Process
sections.body: Premier League chief executive Richard Masters said the sanction remains to be decided and described the ruling as the most significant in the competition’s history. Under league rules, independent commissions can impose fines, points deductions and other sporting sanctions. An Appeal Board can dismiss or allow City’s appeal, or vary the commission’s order, while its proceedings are confidential.

unresolved.text: No sanction or timetable for a sanction decision had been published as of September 29, 2026.
Whether any penalty would apply during the 2026-27 season, affect historic results or survive an appeal remains unresolved.

related_stories.title: Ireland Coach Discusses Uncertainty Ahead of Match Against Israel
related_stories.summary: Heimir Hallgrimsson, the coach of the Republic of Ireland, stated that the team has not yet decided on their approach for the upcoming Nations League match against Israel, which will be played behind closed doors in Serbia. This uncertainty comes amid concerns from some players regarding the ongoing conflict in Gaza.

related_stories.title: Trump to Host AI Summit After Launching America.gov Website
related_stories.summary: President Trump is set to host a summit with leading AI figures in Washington. This follows the launch of America.gov, an AI-powered government website designed to streamline federal services such as passport applications and Medicare enrollment. During the launch event, Trump announced plans to sign an executive order renaming artificial intelligence to 'super intelligence.'

related_stories.title: Tragic Incident in Calais: Child and Two Women Die During Channel Crossing
related_stories.summary: A 10-year-old boy and two women in their thirties died while attempting to cross the English Channel from France. The incident occurred on an overcrowded boat carrying more than 100 people, which faced difficulties off the northern French coast. Authorities reported that the victims were likely trampled during the chaos as passengers sought help.

related_stories.title: Congolese Politician Beaten After Promoting Ebola Awareness
related_stories.summary: Marie-Celestin Karondwa, a politician from the ruling UDPS party in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, was beaten on Sunday after advocating for Ebola awareness during a radio interview. The incident occurred in Butembo, a region experiencing an Ebola outbreak, as residents reacted violently to his message promoting disease prevention measures.
